strengths: Fail-closed member role (thinktin_member). A project transaction cannot see any table that lacks a member policy (vault, private board, plans, inbox, approvals, keys), and column grants hide runs.state_reason, which holds the approval title (executor.rs:2121), plus budget, tokens_used, run_grant_id, events.seq, users.phone and instances.sandbox_address. Of the three, this is the only design where the project-to-private direction is enforced in the database and not by tool code.

thinktin_definer (NOLOGIN NOBYPASSRLS) owns the SECURITY DEFINER functions and reads membership through 'TO thinktin_definer USING (true)' policies. This works under the non-superuser, FORCE-bound thinktin_owner (deploy-checklist.md:57; 0001:435). Because the functions run as a plain role even in the superuser test DB, CI exercises the production path. This fixes the rls-map pitfall instead of assuming it away.

The tenant role is only narrowed. Rows with a project_id are visible only while the user is a current member and outside private_scope, so a member who leaves loses sight of their own agent's project runs, events and inbox at once (projects.md:94). Private-run tools get app.scope=private.

The scope_id = coalesce(project_id, user_id) composite foreign keys keep every run tree homogeneous (one user's private tree, or one project). Private artifacts, board posts and vault requests can only reference private runs. A private run cannot use a project grant, and vice versa. These are constraints, so they bind thinktin_worker, which bypasses RLS.

events_fill derives events.project_id and project_seq from the run and overrides whatever the program passes, so mislabelled events cannot be written. Members page by project_seq, so per-instance seq gaps do not leak private activity.

Revocation works from both sides. via_grant_id joins the ancestor walk, so a revoked lead or creator grant also kills cross-owner child grants. Membership liveness is checked in ancestors_usable!, which the sandbox token and the model gateway share (llmgw.rs:98-114), and token_epoch is bumped on leave.

A clippy disallowed-methods ban on Db::tenant in the orchestrator, covering every tenant call site the design lists (ask.rs:65, board.rs:59/90, delegate.rs:45, peers.rs:47/92, tools.rs:199-313, vault.rs:46/111, executor.rs:802, all verified), forces each tool onto a scoped transaction. The artifact tools that read through the worker are split by Scope.

Per-project HOME, and the private cwd moves to private/ so the private and project trees are siblings. vault_request and schedule tools are kept out of project scope. Vault access is by item id with a foreign key, not by name. A creator's urgent message never interrupts the owner's private run.
flaws: Account erasure cascades through runs_parent_scope ON DELETE CASCADE (A §5.5), so DELETE FROM runs WHERE user_id deletes other owners' child runs, approvals and events. One user's action destroys another user's records. Today's cascade is same-user only (0001:252).

The inbox_items tenant policy hides any row whose project_id is not in app_project_ids(), yet inbox_fill takes the program-supplied project_id for invites and joins. Invite notifications to non-members and 'you were removed/left' notices therefore become invisible to the people they are for.

The tenant role can still INSERT project runs on its own agent, and child runs under another member's project run. FK checks bypass RLS (0001:13-14), and runs_fill only checks agent membership, not that the platform is the writer. The database alone does not enforce 'only the creator/lead dispatches' or protect against injected fake child results.
GRANT SELECT, UPDATE (event_seq) ON project_feeds TO thinktin_app is unnecessary because events_fill runs as definer. It lets a member rewind or skip a project's feed sequence.

Members read agent.tool_call and agent.tool_call_update payloads raw, since there is no DTO trimming (B does trim). For a non-dedicated instance that reads ../private, raw tool output is the easiest exfiltration path.
Project deletion is one synchronous transaction that cascades everything, which risks the worker statement timeout on big projects. A failed delete leaves the project fully readable.

strengths: There are no SECURITY DEFINER membership functions. The policies are TO thinktin_project with uncorrelated EXISTS subqueries, evaluated under the role itself, so behaviour is identical under a superuser test DB and the production thinktin_owner. thinktin_app is not widened.

ProjectActor is a capability token with private fields, built only by locking the projects row and the member row FOR SHARE. Every cross-user worker write needs one, so a missing check fails to compile. The lock order is fixed.

runs_project_guard and run_grants_project_guard reject project runs and project grants unless current_user is in thinktin_worker. They also enforce that the grant and the run share a project, and that a project never changes on UPDATE. This is the only design that blocks tenant-forged project runs and children.

ProjectTx is a separate type, not Tx<R>, so the generic run(), run_tree() and events_after() cannot be called on it. It is read-only (transaction_read_only). Event payloads are trimmed per kind in the DTO, and wait_code is masked to waiting_owner for non-owners.

Correct catch: migrations 0024-0026 'UPDATE run_grants' (0024_peers.sql:13) touch zero rows in production because of FORCE. NO FORCE is done properly for the team copy, and a migration test with a non-superuser owner is planned.
The erasure path detaches cross-owner children (SET NULL) instead of cascade-deleting other users' runs.
flaws: The tenant policy is never narrowed. A member who left still sees, through /v1/runs and the instance event stream, their own agent's project runs and events, including the creator's prompts and other agents' delegated text. This violates projects.md:94 ('退出、被移出的瞬间就看不到了').

The thinktin_project policy on project_members is only 'project_id = app_project_id()'. Setting app.project_id to project Q exposes Q's member list (user_id, role, display_name), so the §2.6 matrix row 'set_config Q → 空' is false. Membership there is enforced in code only.
Deleted projects: status is in no policy, so ProjectTx must reject 'deleted' in code, and the owner's tenant shows project-run plaintext until the purge job runs (acknowledged '最多一分钟').

Private-run tools still use the tenant role, which sees the owner's own project runs. Isolation relies on per-tool exclusions (#9: agent_status, last_finished_run), which fails open for any tool that is forgotten (for example the peers.rs:92 recent_run_events path or run_artifacts).

Shared HOME, and the private cwd stays at the workspace root containing .thinktin/projects/<hex>. Private runs therefore see project files, project sessions inherit root CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md, and Hermes and Claude memory cross both ways. That is weaker than projects.md:65 asks for.

Project vault tools are 'vault_*', which includes vault_request (orchestrator/src/vault.rs:23), when the owner opens the vault. Cross-user content can then drive form popups to the owner. Vault access is granted by item name (text[]), so renaming or re-creating an item silently gains access.
The thinktin_project grant on events includes seq, which leaks gaps in private instance activity inside a run window.

strengths: app_project_ids() is wrapped as an InitPlan and reads only app.user_id, with no user parameter. It runs as the table owner over a non-FORCE project_members table (the blob_purge precedent, 0007:36), so it works under the production owner. A test that reassigns ownership to a NOSUPERUSER role is proposed.

The tenant policy is narrowed for runs, events and artifacts, and DataScope::Private hides every project row from private-run tools. On delete, all members are marked left in the first transaction, so RLS hides everything at once, the owner included, before the async purge.

The cleanest content lifecycle: two-step delete (key destroyed and rows invisible first, plaintext purged in batches later). In phase 9, per-scope workspace archives are encrypted with the project key, so archives stop retaining project files after a crypto-shred.

Per-scope HOME and work directories, private/ moved to a sibling, vault_request and schedule excluded from project scope, IM never forwards project notices, and phone invites return the same answer whatever the phone's status, so they reveal nothing.
flaws: The team-to-project copy (INSERT … SELECT FROM teams, team_members, instances, users, team_templates) runs without NO FORCE. In production, thinktin_owner is FORCE-bound with no policy (0002:102, 0001:435/441, deploy-checklist.md:57), so it copies zero rows silently, which is exactly the rls-map pitfall.

project_read widens thinktin_app SELECT to whole runs rows and all event kinds. Members see state_reason, which is the approval title (executor.rs:2121), tokens_used, budget, run_grant_id, vault.used names (executor.rs:2038-2041), agent.thought and agent.permission_requested. The design explicitly decides '不隐藏'.

DataScope::Project narrows only runs, events, artifacts and projects. Inside a project-run tool, the owner's private board_posts (0025:35), vault_items and vault_requests (0009:55), plans, inbox_items, approvals and instances (0001:436) are all still readable, so the §0.4 claim of a DB-enforced boundary in both directions is false.

events.project_id is a plain column with no derivation trigger. runs.project_id is not immutable: check_run_project allows an UPDATE that moves a run into or out of a project. Nothing in the database ties run_grant_id's project to the run's project. A code bug or tenant SQL can therefore label private events or runs as project content, or the reverse.

Because project_read makes other members' project runs visible, a member's tenant transaction can INSERT a child run under another owner's project run: the invoker trigger finds the parent and the single-column FK passes.

project_members SELECT exposes every member's daily_tokens, total_tokens and consented_at. project_agents.purpose is copied from the owner's private instances.purpose. The migration owner can read project_members because it is not FORCE.
The erased user's project runs (prompts and agent output) are kept indefinitely with user_id pointing at the erased account, a compliance risk the design pushes to the user.

graft: B: In runs_fill and run_grants_fill, reject INSERTs with project_id NOT NULL unless pg_has_role(current_user,'thinktin_worker','USAGE'), or add 'project_id IS NULL' to the thinktin_app WITH CHECK. This stops tenant-forged project runs and children under other owners' runs.

B: Make ProjectActor a capability type (private fields, built only by locking the projects and member rows FOR SHARE) and require it in every cross-user Tx<Worker> write, on top of A's project_role_of SQL checks.

B: Per-kind payload trimming in the member DTO (tool_call keeps only id, title, kind and status) and wait_code masking to waiting_owner for non-owners. Also set transaction_read_only on project-scope read transactions.
B: On erasure, cancel and then detach cross-owner children (parent_run_id SET NULL) instead of letting runs_parent_scope ON DELETE CASCADE delete other owners' runs.

B: A migration test that runs the 0032 copy, and any backfill, under a non-superuser owner. Write the rule into release docs: future 'UPDATE run_grants' platform-tool backfills (the 0024-0026 pattern) need the NO FORCE dance and 'AND project_id IS NULL'.

C: Two-step delete. One short transaction destroys the key, revokes grants, cancels runs and makes the project invisible in RLS, either by marking members left or by checking status in app_project_id. Plaintext is purged in batches afterwards, so a large project cannot hit the worker statement timeout and stay readable.
C: Phase-9 per-scope workspace archives sealed with the project key (separate AAD domain), so the crypto-shred also covers ACS/OSS archives and their cleanup no longer needs to wake the sandbox.
C: A store test that reassigns all table and function ownership to a temporary NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS role and re-runs the membership checks, in addition to A's definer-ownership assertions.
C: An AAD domain-separation test showing that a user-DEK-sealed artifact cannot be opened as a project artifact, and that project reads never fall back to the user DEK.
must_fix: Every design: block tenant-forged project runs at the DB level. FK checks bypass RLS (0001_init.sql:13-14), so in A and C a member's tenant transaction can INSERT a run with project_id=P, or a child under another owner's project run. A's runs_fill and C's check_run_project only verify agent membership. Require the worker role for project runs and project grants (B's runs_project_guard pattern).

A: runs_parent_scope ON DELETE CASCADE plus 'DELETE FROM runs WHERE user_id' (users.rs:200) cascade-deletes other owners' child runs, approvals and events when one member erases their account. Today the cascade at 0001_init.sql:252 is same-user only. Detach cross-owner children instead.

A: the inbox_items tenant policy hides rows whose project_id is not in app_project_ids(), but inbox_fill keeps the program-supplied project_id for invites and joins (A §2.5). Invitees and removed members can never see their notices. Write those rows with project_id NULL, or keep the project link in a column that RLS does not filter on.
A: drop 'GRANT UPDATE (event_seq) ON project_feeds TO thinktin_app'. events_fill is SECURITY DEFINER, so the tenant role never needs it, and the grant lets members corrupt project_seq ordering.

B: the tenant policy must be narrowed so that a member's own project-run rows disappear when they leave. Otherwise /v1/runs and instance events keep showing project content after leaving, violating docs/projects.md:94. B §2.1 keeps tenant '没放宽' and never adds a membership condition.

B: the thinktin_project policy on project_members ('project_id = app_project_id()') has no membership check. Setting app.project_id to project Q reveals Q's member list, so the §2.6 matrix claim is wrong. Add a membership-checked path or explicitly accept and test it.

B: deleted projects are hidden from members only by a ProjectTx check in code; no policy looks at status. The owner's tenant shows project-run plaintext until purge. Put the status or membership check into the policies, or hide rows synchronously on delete.

B: keep vault_request out of project scope. VAULT_TOOLS is ['vault_list','vault_request'] (crates/orchestrator/src/vault.rs:23), and B grants 'vault_*' whenever the owner enables the vault, so cross-user content could push forms to the owner. Key vault access on item ids, not names.

C: the team copy in 0031 runs INSERT … SELECT over FORCE tables (teams and team_members FORCE at 0002_collaboration.sql:102, instances at 0001_init.sql:435, users at 0001_init.sql:441) as the non-superuser thinktin_owner (deploy-checklist.md:57), so it silently copies zero rows in production. Wrap the copy in NO FORCE / FORCE, as A and B do.

C: the project_read policy gives thinktin_app full runs rows and all event kinds. That leaks state_reason (approval title, set at executor.rs:2121), vault.used item names (executor.rs:2038-2041), agent.thought, agent.permission_requested, tokens_used and budget to other members. Use column grants and an event-kind whitelist under a dedicated role.

C: DataScope::Project leaves the owner's private board_posts (0025_board.sql:35), vault_items and vault_requests (0009_vault.sql:55), and plans, inbox_items, approvals and instances (0001_init.sql:436) readable from project-run tools, so the boundary claim in §0.4 is false. A fail-closed role, as in A, is needed.

C: derive events.project_id (and approvals and inbox project_id) in a trigger from the run, make runs.project_id immutable on UPDATE, and enforce in the database that run_grant_id's project equals the run's project. As designed, these are program-supplied and mutable.

strengths: Fail-closed member boundary: a separate thinktin_member role only has 'current project' policies, so any table without one stays invisible. Existing tenant code (runs.rs run/run_tree, instances.rs peers, gateway runs.rs:185-221 cancel?tree) needs no audit.

Avoids the production-owner pitfall in a way CI actually exercises. Definer functions are owned by thinktin_definer, a plain NOLOGIN NOBYPASSRLS role reading through TO-definer policies, so the superuser test DB (testing.rs, setup-db.sh:16-18) still runs them as a normal role.

The scope_id = coalesce(project_id, user_id) composite FK makes a run tree all-private or all-one-project in the DB. Re-pointing artifacts/board_posts/vault_requests at runs(id, scope_id) keeps private content off project runs. Verified: a GENERATED column cannot be used here (PG16: 'invalid ON DELETE action for foreign key constraint containing generated column').
The narrowed tenant policy enforces 'leaving makes it invisible' even for the owner's own project runs, and Db::private_scope hides project rows from private-run tools (projects.md section 9, 8.15).

Best phasing for shipping one phase at a time. P1 is boundary-only with no feature. A projects.cross_user server flag stays off until P7 and the 15.7 review. The test plan includes a three-user matrix, forged-write cases, a production-owner assertion and a stronger coverage test.

Cited facts check out: 0001:249-253 FKs, deploy-checklist.md:55-71, executor.rs:739-818, lock_run_waits runs.rs:428, list_runs and the 0020 partial indexes, bridge.rs:416 100-byte limit (94 bytes computed), hub.rs:82, error.rs:66-79.
flaws: Heaviest P1 churn. It swaps FKs on ~9 tables (runs, plans, run_grants, events, approvals, inbox_items, artifacts, board_posts, vault_requests). It does NO FORCE backfills and rewrites policies on 6 tables, adds two new roles with deploy-checklist changes, and adds UNIQUE(id, scope_id) indexes on runs and plans.

Hot path: events_fill is a SECURITY DEFINER plpgsql trigger (with a SET clause) on every append_event (events.rs:40-72). For project runs it also takes a per-project project_feeds row lock held to commit. write_event runs per log chunk (executor.rs:1241-1256), so all agents in a project serialize their logs. A transaction that appends and then locks another instance of the same project can deadlock.

No index for the project feed reads. events has only its PK (instance_id, seq, created_at) and events_run (0001:271-283), so project_events_after/project_event_range on (project_id, project_seq) scan every partition.
Replacing the (run_id, user_id) FKs on approvals and events with (run_id, scope_id) drops the 'row owner = run owner' guarantee from 0001:281,342. A keeps both FKs only for run_grants.
Erasure: runs_parent_scope ON DELETE CASCADE plus DELETE FROM runs WHERE user_id (users.rs:200) also deletes other members' child runs. The design only parks this as user question 4.
Misses ensure_instance_grant (gateway routes/runs.rs:67-90). A top-level, plan-less project grant visible to the tenant would count as the private grant, so 'stop all' recovery breaks.
clippy.toml disallowing Db::tenant in orchestrator breaks CI (ci.yml:57 uses -D warnings with --all-targets): crates/orchestrator/tests/*.rs use tenant ~100 times.

thinktin_app gets no writes on project tables, but adopt_in needs Tx<Tenant> (control/src/lib.rs:216) and template adopt is one transaction today (routes/teams.rs:183-226). The design does not say how adoption stays atomic.

Minor: tenant UPDATE(event_seq) on project_feeds is unnecessary (the trigger runs as definer) and lets members inflate the counter. GRANT thinktin_definer TO CURRENT_USER does not catch unique_violation when parallel test DBs run migrations. Making thinktin_owner a member of thinktin_definer gives the migration account read access through USING(true), which contradicts section 1.3.

strengths: Least churn and lowest regression risk. thinktin_app tenant policies on runs, events and instances are untouched. Only the parent FK is relaxed (single-column FK plus guard trigger); the instance/grant/plan composite FKs stay. Every existing tenant read-then-act flow behaves the same.

No SECURITY DEFINER at all. thinktin_project policies use uncorrelated EXISTS on project_members, and project_members' own policy is project_id = app_project_id(), so there is no recursion. It works identically under the superuser test DB and the non-superuser production owner.

ProjectTx is a separate type rather than Tx<R>, so the generic Tx<R> helpers (runs.rs:317-337, events.rs:76-110) cannot be called on it at compile time. The ProjectActor capability token (private fields, created only after locking the project and member rows) plus a fixed lock order covers worker-side cross-user writes.
Cheap hot path: events_project and runs_project_guard are SECURITY INVOKER triggers with a PK lookup and no counter lock. The curated project feed is written explicitly in the triggering transaction.

pg_has_role(current_user, 'thinktin_worker', 'USAGE') in the guards means a tenant can never insert project runs or project grants. The grant fallbacks in both places (active_grant_for_instance, ensure_instance_grant) exclude project grants.

Careful migration handling: NO FORCE copy in 0031, a re-copy of teams created during the rollout window in 0032, and a correct observation that the 0024-0026 UPDATE run_grants backfills are silent no-ops in production under FORCE.

The new 'project' run source fits the existing known_sources() rollout gate (runs.rs:201-205, 880), so older executors skip project root tasks. Adds the delegate_stop tool the product requires (projects.md section 7).
flaws: Owner-side visibility after leaving is not enforced. With tenant policies unchanged, a member who leaves still sees their own agents' project runs and events through /v1/runs and the instance streams, including other members' prompts and results. This violates projects.md section 9 and 8.15 ('退出即不可见').

Private-run tools (peers.rs:47/92, recent_run_events events.rs:116) see the owner's project runs under tenant. Keeping project content out of private sessions depends on explicit per-call filters (table item #9), which fails open.
The thinktin_project policy on project_members is only project_id = app_project_id(). The matrix claim that switching app.project_id to Q returns empty is false for project_members.
ProjectTx::run_events grants and exposes the per-instance seq. B's own section 7.4 says seq gaps leak the owner's private activity.

Weaker session isolation: shared HOME, and the project dir .thinktin/projects/<hex> sits under the private cwd '.'. Private runs can see project files, and project sessions read workspace-root CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md.

Erasure deletes the erased member's project runs, leaving other members' children with parent_run_id NULL and a dangling root_run_id. Only roots get the 'project' source, so project child runs (delegate/ask/pipeline sources) can still be claimed by older executors during a rollout.
Phase 3 is very large: executor, shim, llm-gw, auth, catalog and cross-user creator dispatch land together. There is no cross-user feature flag.

strengths: Project keys plus project-owned board and artifacts, with a full content-lifecycle table (leave, erase, delete). The two-step delete (keys destroyed and all members marked left in one transaction, then a background batched purge) avoids the 60s statement limit when erasure deletes several projects.

The lazy project-event sequencer (write with seq NULL, number committed rows under the head lock just before reading) keeps counter locks off the write path and avoids instance/feed deadlocks. Its reasoning about never missing rows is correct.
Keeps the erased member's project runs as contributions (users.rs:200 gets AND project_id IS NULL), which matches projects.md section 10.
Single application role with no new login grants. The ENABLE-but-not-FORCE project_members follows the real blob_purge precedent (0007:32-38).
Points out the INSERT ... RETURNING snapshot problem with STABLE membership functions. Handles ensure_instance_grant and active_grant_for_instance.
flaws: Team data copy in 0031 has no NO FORCE handling. In production the migration owner sees zero rows (0001:432-436 FORCE with policies TO thinktin_app only, deploy-checklist.md:55-71), so installed test builds lose their teams. The join to users is affected the same way.

0032 puts several CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY statements in one '-- no-transaction' file. sqlx sends the file as one simple query, which Postgres runs as an implicit transaction block. Verified on PG16: 'CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY cannot run inside a transaction block'. The migration, and therefore every test, fails.

events.project_id is added but never populated. There is no trigger, and append_event (events.rs:40-72) does not set it. Policies depend on it, so events written by older replicas or forgotten code paths are treated as private.

project_read broadens thinktin_app on runs, events and artifacts, so every existing tenant read without a user_id filter now returns other members' rows with full columns. Events carry no kind whitelist, which exposes agent.thought, agent.permission_requested, vault.used and agent.vault_reveal (executor.rs:2037-2042, shim.rs:135) plus the per-instance seq.

The claim that DataScope blocks both directions at the DB level is overstated. instances, plans, board_posts, vault_items, approvals and inbox_items keep the plain tenant policy, so tenant_in(Project) still sees the owner's private rows.

The production-owner test uses REASSIGN OWNED, which also reassigns shared objects such as databases owned by the superuser test role, cluster-wide while tests run in parallel. It should use targeted ALTER ... OWNER.
project_agent_auth has no (project_id, instance_id, user_id) FK to project_agents, yet thinktin_app gets INSERT on it.
Ten phases. Phase 1 is huge (RLS rewrite, keys, read routes, FFI), and phase 9 (per-scope workspace archives) adds scope beyond WBS 8.13-8.19.

graft: B: Make the member transaction a separate type (ProjectTx) instead of Tx<Member>. Generic impl<R> Tx<R> helpers then fail to compile instead of failing at runtime with 42501 column errors.

B: ProjectActor capability token (private fields, built only by Tx<Worker>::project_actor, which locks the projects row FOR SHARE and the member row FOR SHARE) as a required parameter of every cross-user worker write. Also B's fixed lock order: projects, member, project_agent, runs, instances, feed.
B: SECURITY INVOKER events trigger that only copies project_id from runs and takes no counter lock. Do not allocate a per-project seq inside append_event.

B: In ensure_instance_grant (routes/runs.rs:67-90), filter project_id IS NULL in addition to active_grant_for_instance.

B: Note in release.md and code that 0024-0026-style UPDATE run_grants backfills are no-ops in production under FORCE. Future grant backfills must use NO FORCE and add AND project_id IS NULL.
B: Re-copy teams created by older replicas during the rollout window in the following migration before the old tables are retired.

Otherwise the production owner, a non-superuser bound by FORCE with policies TO thinktin_app (0001:432-436, deploy-checklist.md:55-71), copies zero rows and installed iOS/Android test builds lose their teams.

Reproduced on PG16: 'CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY cannot run inside a transaction block'. Split into one file per index, or use plain CREATE INDEX since there is no production data.
C: Populate events.project_id (and approvals and inbox_items) in a BEFORE INSERT trigger from runs. append_event (events.rs:40-72) never sets it, and C's tenant/project_read policies depend on it.

A: Add an index for member feed reads, e.g. CREATE INDEX events_project ON events (project_id, project_seq) WHERE project_id IS NOT NULL. Today events has only PK (instance_id, seq, created_at) and events_run (0001:271-283), so project_events_after scans every partition.

A: Move per-project sequencing off append_event. events_fill locks project_feeds on every project event, and write_event commits once per log chunk (executor.rs:1241-1256). That serializes all agents in a project and can deadlock: tx1 appends on instance X (locking X, then F) and then locks instance Y via bump_epochs_where or append, while tx2 holds Y and waits for F.

A: Keep the original (run_id, user_id) FKs on approvals and events alongside the new (run_id, scope_id) ones (0001:281,342), as A already does for run_grants. Otherwise approvals or events on a project run can carry a different member's user_id and become visible to that member under the tenant policy.

A: Erasure must not cascade-delete other owners' child runs. With runs_parent_scope ON DELETE CASCADE, DELETE FROM runs WHERE user_id = $1 (users.rs:200) deletes them, which contradicts projects.md section 10. Detach or retain them instead.

A: Filter project grants out of ensure_instance_grant (gateway routes/runs.rs:67-90, `.any(|g| g.plan_id.is_none() && g.parent_id.is_none())`). Otherwise, after 'stop all', a visible project grant blocks reissuing the private grant.

A: The orchestrator clippy.toml disallowing store::Db::tenant needs a crate-level #![allow(clippy::disallowed_methods)] in crates/orchestrator/tests/*.rs (about 100 uses). CI runs `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` (.github/workflows/ci.yml:57).

A: Specify how template adopt stays atomic. thinktin_app has no project-table writes, but control::adopt_in requires Tx<Tenant> (control/src/lib.rs:216) and adoption plus team creation is one transaction today (routes/teams.rs:183-226). Use B's tenant create_solo policies or an explicit compensating delete.

A: Drop the tenant UPDATE(event_seq) grant on project_feeds, since the definer trigger does the update. Catch unique_violation in the DO-block GRANT thinktin_definer TO CURRENT_USER, because test DBs migrate concurrently and roles are cluster-wide (0001:8). Note that thinktin_owner's membership in thinktin_definer gives the migration account read access to runs and instances through the USING(true) policies.

B: Narrow the tenant policy on runs, events, approvals and inbox_items so project rows need current membership. This needs no definer, because the tenant can read its own project_members rows: `project_id IS NULL OR project_id = ANY (ARRAY(SELECT project_id FROM project_members WHERE user_id = app_user_id() AND left_at IS NULL))`. Without it a leaving owner still sees their agents' project runs (projects.md section 9, 8.15).

B: Scope private-run tools at the DB level (A's app.scope=private, or C's DataScope::Private). peers.rs:47/92 and recent_run_events (events.rs:116) otherwise read the owner's project runs into private sessions.

B: Fix or retract the matrix claim that set_config('app.project_id', Q) returns empty. thinktin_project's project_members policy is only project_id = app_project_id(), so Q's member list is readable. Also stop granting events.seq to thinktin_project (run_events), because B's own section 7.4 says seq gaps leak private activity.

All: Add a rollout gate so older executors never execute project runs. claim_next_run filters only by known_sources() (runs.rs:201-205, 880). A and C create project runs with existing sources ('user', 'delegate', 'ask'), and B does the same for project children. An older replica would therefore claim them and run them with the private cwd and HOME and the private-grant fallback (executor.rs:738-746). Add project_id IS NULL to claim and takeover from the phase that adds the column until the executing phase.
